olderDemand.summary: Reporter describes two agents interleaving shared stash pushes and popping each other's work. Demonstrates stash identity and intended destination are practical problems.
Reporter describes an agent popping an older shared stash after a no-change stash command, contaminating its worktree. Older context, not November 3 evidence.

ideas.name: StashScope
ideas.concept: Read-only stash-to-worktree evidence matrix: stable stash SHA, touched paths, base/stashed/destination committed blob IDs and modes, dirty paths and untracked collisions. No application or claim of actual merge prediction.
ideas.demand: Directly related to November 3 Worktrunk move-changes stash failure fix; older independent shared-stash incidents.
ideas.distinctValue: Cross-worktree destination comparison with stable identity and explainable metadata. Reviewed stash tools focus on browsing and actions in the current working directory.
ideas.demo: Tiny real temporary repository with multiple worktrees, an existing stash, a divergent destination, a dirty destination and a new-file collision; clearly label demonstration as generated.
ideas.discoverability: Concrete 'which worktree fits this stash?' pitch for Git/worktree/agent users; complements Worktrunk rather than replacing it.
ideas.risks: Snapshot is not atomic and does not prove safe application, ownership, intended branch, merge outcome or complete recovery. Should expose unknowns and unsupported states.

ideas.name: Worktree overlap map
ideas.concept: Compare committed, dirty and untracked path/hunk overlap across linked worktrees.
ideas.demand: Worktrunk appeared in Nov3 archive and yesterday direct Trending; parallel worktree friction is concrete.
ideas.distinctValue: Low without a stronger niche: Grove already does shared-base file/hunk/symbol/schema analysis, TUI and JSON/CI; herdr-collide includes dirty work and real merge prediction.
ideas.discoverability: Broad problem but crowded direct competition; new basic version weaker than established tools.

ideas.name: Worktree preflight doctor
ideas.concept: Read-only inventory of unfinished operations, stale metadata, markers and potential cleanup hazards.
ideas.demand: November3 Worktrunk4683 reports markers surviving removed worktrees/branches.
ideas.distinctValue: Low for a general doctor: Tinkora already checks pointers, commondir, prunable/locked states, config and tracked status; Worktrunk has rich status.
ideas.demo: Easy synthetic broken-topology fixture but careful platform compatibility required.
ideas.discoverability: Clear search intent, however overlaps existing diagnostics and risks becoming a thin status wrapper.

competitors.observedCapability: TUI displays stash contents and offers apply/pop/drop. README explicitly says it warns when a stash does not apply cleanly to the current working directory.
competitors.difference: StashScope focuses on comparing a stable stash identity against multiple linked worktrees using explained metadata; no mutate actions.

competitors.observedCapability: Rust stash manager TUI; list, diff, files, apply/pop/drop/new and fuzzy search.
competitors.difference: No cross-worktree compatibility matrix documented in reviewed README.

competitors.observedCapability: Stash list and diff preview with drop confirmation.
competitors.difference: No destination evidence comparison documented in reviewed README.

competitors.observedCapability: Shared-base file/hunk/symbol/dependency/schema overlap detection; background daemon, TUI, JSON and CI mode.
competitors.difference: Direct reason to reject generic overlap map.

competitors.observedCapability: Read-only worktree pairing and temporary merge prediction with dirty work, Herdr integration and one-shot JSON.
competitors.difference: Direct reason to reject generic overlap map.

competitors.observedCapability: Finds overlap in declared path inventories and emits Mermaid; does not inspect Git.
competitors.difference: More limited than live inspection but still a relevant overlap-map alternative.

competitors.observedCapability: Offline read-only topology/metadata doctor with optional tracked-status checks.
competitors.difference: Reason to reject general worktree doctor.

searchLimitations: Repository searches were not exhaustive; absence in reviewed README is not proof a capability never exists. No stars promised. Today's rolling Trending snapshot is separate (rolling-observation.json).
